title: Structured output

ground.note: The brief: provider facts checked on 2026-10-27, the operator's settled decisions, the calls in scope and the out-of-scope list.

The prerequisite spec: one session outcome per ended session (an answer or a failure with kind, provider message and session id); `error_max_structured_output_retries` is a `provider-error`; its reader keeps the answer side open to a structured answer.
runAgent, resumeAgentSession and complete return `finalText`; AgentRunOptions.readOnly keeps a Claude Code session to its reading tools.
Every Claude Code call runs `--print --output-format stream-json --verbose`; resumes add `--resume <id>`; sealed completions add `--no-session-persistence` and `--tools ""`.
Codex runs `codex exec -C <cwd> …` and resumes with `codex exec resume <id> …`; readOnly is honoured.
Vibe runs with `--output streaming` and resumes with `--resume <id>`; it has no schema option.
The corrective resume: a refused final message is resumed once in the same session with the refusal; a second refusal is `<kind> document rejected twice — first answer: …; retry: …`.
Headless spec and plan authoring: runAgent, decode spec-document or plan-document, one corrective resume.
The plan-extraction fallback: a sealed `complete` call pinned to Claude Code, no session; the prompt allows a `{"error": …}` answer that its JSON Schema does not describe; no retry.
decide's headless handback resumes the interactive session and decodes a revised document or a hand-decision-answer, with one corrective resume.
The `decide --verdicts` writer: runAgent or resume, decode, one corrective resume, output.jsonl and retry-output.jsonl.
The interactive first turn: runAgent, decode the first-reading answer, one corrective resume.
The interactive closing turn: resume, decode the interactive-handoff answer, one corrective resume.
hand-decision-answer is a root union of a spec variant and a plan variant, exported with JSONSchema.make: the shape Codex strict refuses at the root.
ExtractionAnswerSchema: `version: 1`, run, phases; no variant for the incomplete-plan report.
`phax review-code --headless` decodes a version-1 code-review answer with no retry; a refused answer exits 1 with `Code review failed: answer refused: … To retry, run: …`.

The compliance session writes compliance-review.md and .json into `.phax-context/`; phax copies the Markdown as is; a missing, unparsable or undecodable JSON becomes verdict `unknown`; no retry; the session is not read-only.
The prompt asks for free Markdown (verdict, per-phase findings, unplanned-change ledger, unmet-promise ledger, attention points) and a version-1 JSON verdict holding neither ledger.
The answer carries `version: 1`; compliance-review.json carries `$schema` (stamp 0.17.0) then verdict, summary, perPhase, attentionPoints, pointers; unknown keys refused.
`phax review-compliance <run>` prints `Verdict: unknown` when the JSON was missing or refused, and `Compliance review failed: … To retry, run: …` with exit 1 on a failure.
PHAX_RELEASE is 0.29.0; compliance-review is stamped 0.17.0, hand-decision-answer 0.25.0, code-review is born at 0.29.0.

context:
Prerequisite: this spec builds on the spec "Provider failures", which reads every ended agent session into one session outcome (an answer, or a failure with its kind, the provider message and the session id). This spec extends the answer side of that outcome to a structured answer.

Eight agent calls must return a structured answer that phax decodes: headless authoring of specs and plans, the plan-extraction fallback, decide's headless handback after an interactive session, the `decide --verdicts` writer, the interactive first turn, the interactive closing turn, the headless code review (`phax review-code --headless`, whose plan is running now) and the compliance review. Today every one of them states the answer's JSON Schema in the prompt text, reads the session's final text, parses it as JSON and decodes it with phax's own schema. Except for extraction, the code review and the compliance review, a refused answer resumes the session once with the refusal; a second refusal fails the command.

Three calls depart from that. The plan-extraction fallback is a sealed completion with no session; its prompt allows a `{"error": "<what is missing>"}` answer that its schema does not describe, and it has no retry. The headless code review has no retry either. The compliance review does not answer at all: its session writes compliance-review.md (free prose: verdict, per-phase findings, an unplanned-change ledger, an unmet-promise ledger, attention points) and compliance-review.json (a version-1 verdict holding neither ledger) into `.phax-context/` of the worktree. phax copies the Markdown verbatim into the run folder; a missing, unparsable or undecodable JSON silently becomes `Verdict: unknown`.

The providers, checked on 2026-10-27: Claude Code 2.1.311 takes `--json-schema <schema>` inline with `--print`, delivers the answer as `structured_output` on the result event, and fails with subtype `error_max_structured_output_retries` when it cannot meet the schema; whether it combines with `--resume`, `--tools` and stream-json is not documented. Codex 0.153.4 takes `--output-schema <FILE>` on `exec` and `exec resume` and sends it with `strict: true`, so OpenAI's strict subset applies (closed objects with every key required, no root `anyOf`/`oneOf`, a limited keyword set). Mistral Vibe 3.0.3 has no schema option.
problem:
A wrong key, a wrong enum value, a wrong id or a missing `$schema` costs phax a whole session or a corrective turn, because the provider never sees the answer's schema as a constraint: the model reads it as prompt text and phax finds the mistake only once the session has ended. Both providers phax runs most can enforce a schema while generating, and phax does not use it.

The compliance review is worse off. Its JSON verdict has no retry, and a bad or missing file is reported as `Verdict: unknown` with no reason, after a full review session has been paid for. Its Markdown is free prose the agent writes to disk, so it can disagree with the verdict, and the session needs write access for a review that should only read. The headless code review refuses its answer with no second chance, and the extraction fallback's incomplete-plan report sits outside its own schema, so no schema-enforcing provider could ever return it.

productGoal.statement: Every agent call that returns a structured answer hands the provider a schema it enforces while generating, wherever the provider can, so shape mistakes are corrected by the provider inside the session instead of costing a corrective turn or a refused session. The provider schema is derived from the answer's full schema, never written by hand, and phax's own decoder, with the coherence checks no schema can express, stays the final judge on every provider. The compliance review becomes a structured answer like the others: read-only, with its corrective resume, and with both its files written by phax from the answer.
productGoal.guidingRule: The provider may shape the answer; only phax's decoder accepts it.

terminology.definition: The JSON document an agent call must return for phax to decode: spec-document, plan-document, the extraction answer, a revised document or hand-decision-answer, decide-verdicts, first-reading, interactive-handoff, code-review and compliance-review.
The structured answer's published schema as phax's decoder enforces it, as `phax artifact schema` and packages/schemas export it.

A check phax's decoder runs beyond the full schema, against the call's context: a criterion id exists in the source spec's sidecar, a verdict moves only presented questions, a revision names the sections it touches, a phase id is a phase of the run.
The full schema plus the call's coherence checks; the only judge of whether an answer is accepted.
The schema phax hands the provider for one structured answer: derived from the full schema to fit the stricter of Claude Code's and Codex's rules (Codex strict), shared by both providers.
A provider enforcing the provider schema while the model generates: Claude Code's `--json-schema`, Codex's `--output-schema`.
The one resume of the same session that names phax's decoder refusal and asks for the whole answer again; a second refusal fails the call.
The test that keeps every provider schema inside both Claude Code's and Codex strict's accepted rules.
The compliance answer's list of files touched beyond the plan, each with its phase and the reviewer's note.
The compliance answer's list of promised tests or artifacts the reviewer did not find, each with its phase and note.

requirements.title: Native structured output on Claude Code and Codex
requirements.statement: WHERE a structured answer is asked of Claude Code or Codex THE system SHALL hand that provider the answer's provider schema, on the first session and on its corrective resume, for each of the eight calls: headless spec and plan authoring, the plan-extraction fallback, decide's headless handback, the `decide --verdicts` writer, the interactive first turn, the interactive closing turn, the headless code review and the compliance review.

requirements.title: Mistral Vibe keeps the schema in the prompt
requirements.statement: WHERE a structured answer is asked of Mistral Vibe THE system SHALL state the answer's full schema in the prompt and judge the answer with phax's decoder and the corrective resume, as it does today.

requirements.title: The provider schema is derived
requirements.statement: The system shall derive each provider schema from the answer's full schema, never from a hand-written one, as one closed object with every key required, no lookahead pattern, no root `anyOf` or `oneOf`, and `$schema` as a `const` wherever the answer carries a `$schema`.

requirements.title: The provider schema never tightens
requirements.statement: The system shall make each provider schema accept every answer that the full schema accepts for the variant the call expects.

requirements.title: The schema check
requirements.statement: IF a provider schema uses a construct outside Codex's strict subset or outside what Claude Code's `--json-schema` accepts THEN the schema check SHALL fail, naming the answer and the construct.

requirements.title: The structured answer is what is decoded
requirements.statement: WHEN a provider returns the answer as native structured output THE system SHALL decode that structured output, not the session's final text.

requirements.title: phax's decoder is the final judge
requirements.statement: The system shall accept a structured answer only once phax's decoder, full schema and coherence checks included, has accepted it, whatever the provider and whether or not the provider enforced a schema.

requirements.title: One corrective resume on a decoder refusal
requirements.statement: WHEN phax's decoder refuses the answer of a call that has a session THE system SHALL resume that session once with the refusal, handing the same provider schema where r-native applies, and fail the call on a second refusal.

requirements.title: A provider that cannot meet the schema
requirements.statement: IF the provider ends a session because the answer could not meet the provider schema (Claude Code's `error_max_structured_output_retries`) THEN the system SHALL report that session failure as the Provider failures spec reports a `provider-error`, and SHALL NOT run the corrective resume.

requirements.title: The headless code review gains its corrective resume
requirements.statement: WHEN phax refuses the first answer of `phax review-code --headless` THE system SHALL print the refusal and resume the session once, instead of failing at the first refusal.

requirements.title: The extraction's incomplete-plan report is in its schema
requirements.statement: WHEN the plan-extraction answer reports the plan incomplete, in the shape its full schema describes, THE system SHALL fail the extraction naming what the answer says is missing.

requirements.title: The compliance review answers
requirements.statement: The system shall take the compliance review's result from the session's structured answer, and shall not read any file the session writes.

requirements.title: The compliance session is read-only
requirements.statement: The system shall run the compliance review session read-only, as it runs headless authoring and decide's handback.

requirements.title: phax writes both compliance files
requirements.statement: WHEN phax accepts a compliance answer THE system SHALL write compliance-review.json and compliance-review.md in the run folder, rendering the Markdown from the answer alone.

requirements.title: The ledgers are answer fields
requirements.statement: The system shall require in every compliance answer an unplanned-change ledger and an unmet-promise ledger, each a possibly empty list.

requirements.title: The compliance answer covers the run's phases
requirements.statement: IF a compliance answer's per-phase verdicts name a phase that is not a phase of the run, or omit or repeat one of the run's phases, THEN phax's decoder SHALL refuse the answer, naming the phase.

requirements.title: A refused compliance review is a failure
requirements.statement: IF the compliance answer is refused after its corrective resume THEN the system SHALL report the compliance review failed, naming both refusals, write neither compliance file nor a records entry, and SHALL NOT report a verdict `unknown`.

requirements.title: compliance-review.json at 0.29.0
requirements.statement: The system shall stamp compliance-review.json and the compliance answer with `$schema` at 0.29.0, carrying the two ledgers as required fields, and shall refuse a 0.29.0 compliance review that lacks either ledger.

surface.summary: A compliance review whose answer is wrong gets one more chance in the same session, and when it still fails phax says why instead of showing an unknown verdict.
surface.before:
$ phax review-compliance audio-export
Verdict: unknown
Compliance review: ~/.phax/runs/notebook.audio-export/compliance-review.md
surface.after:
$ phax review-compliance audio-export
⚠ compliance-review answer refused — perPhase: phase "phase-04" is not a phase of this run
  resuming the session once to ask for the whole answer again
Verdict: conformant-with-deviations
Compliance review: ~/.phax/runs/notebook.audio-export/compliance-review.md
Recorded: notebook.audio-export/compliance-review (3fa91c0d)

$ phax review-compliance audio-export
✗ Compliance review failed: compliance-review answer rejected twice — first answer: perPhase: phase "phase-02" is missing; retry: perPhase: phase "phase-02" is missing. To retry, run: phax review-compliance audio-export
$? = 1

surface.summary: The compliance review now lists the files changed beyond the plan and the promised tests that are missing, alongside its verdict.
surface.before:
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/compliance-review/0.17.0.json",
  "verdict": "conformant-with-deviations",
  "summary": "All four phases delivered; phase-02 skipped one promised test.",
  "perPhase": [ … ],
  "attentionPoints": [ "Confirm the retry backoff with the audio team." ],
  "pointers": []
}

surface.summary: The compliance review's Markdown is written by phax from the review itself, so it always matches the verdict and keeps the same sections from run to run.
surface.before: (free prose written by the review agent, in its own layout)
surface.after:
# Compliance review — notebook.audio-export

Verdict: conformant-with-deviations

All four phases delivered; phase-02 skipped one promised test.

## phase-02 — conformant-with-deviations

- tests · deviation — The promised integration test for export retries is missing.

## Unplanned changes

- phase-02 · src/export/backoff.ts — Shared helper, justified in the handoff.

## Unmet promises

- phase-02 · integration test: export retries on 503 — Not found in tests/integration.

## Attention points

- Confirm the retry backoff with the audio team.

## Pointers

None.

surface.summary: The extraction model reports an incomplete plan inside the answer's own schema, so a schema-enforcing provider can return it.
surface.before:
{ "version": 1, "run": { … }, "phases": [ … ] }
{ "error": "phase-03: the Test strategy item 'covers retries' is not in the line format" }   (outside the schema)
surface.after:
{ "version": 2, "plan": { "run": { … }, "phases": [ … ] }, "incomplete": null }
{ "version": 2, "plan": null, "incomplete": "phase-03: the Test strategy item 'covers retries' is not in the line format" }

nonGoals: Interactive sessions, phase turns, fix attempts and the windows probe: they return no structured answer.
The external providers (oracles, brief, architecture, plan auditor): their requests and answers keep their own contracts.
The phase handoff: it stays Markdown written by the phase; making it a structured answer is a later spec, because every later phase reads it.
The rest of the Mistral Vibe V3 review, including whether `--enabled-tools` makes Vibe honour `readOnly`: Vibe ignores `readOnly` as it does today.
A corrective turn for the plan-extraction fallback: it stays a sealed completion with no session and one attempt.
More than one corrective resume, or a corrective resume after a session failure: a provider failure is reported as the Provider failures spec reports it.
Hand-written provider schemas, or any change to a full schema other than the compliance review's and the extraction answer's.
Reading compliance-review files the session writes, or keeping the agent's own Markdown prose: phax writes both files.
Back-compat for compliance-review.json: a 0.29.0 file without the ledgers is refused, never defaulted.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Claude Code gets the provider schema, on the resume too
acceptanceCriteria.given: a headless spec authoring session on Claude Code whose first answer phax's decoder refuses
acceptanceCriteria.then: both the first session's and the corrective resume's argv carry `--json-schema` with the spec-document provider schema, and the resume carries `--resume` with the first session's id

acceptanceCriteria.name: Codex gets the provider schema on exec and exec resume
acceptanceCriteria.given: a `decide --verdicts` writer routed to Codex whose first answer is refused
acceptanceCriteria.then: `codex exec` and `codex exec resume` each carry `--output-schema` naming a file whose content is the decide-verdicts provider schema

acceptanceCriteria.name: Every structured call hands a provider schema
acceptanceCriteria.given: each of the eight structured calls run against a recording fake of Claude Code and of Codex
acceptanceCriteria.then: each spawn carries that answer's provider schema, and no call that returns no structured answer (phase turn, fix turn, windows probe) carries one

acceptanceCriteria.name: Vibe keeps the prompt schema and the corrective resume
acceptanceCriteria.given: a compliance review routed to Mistral Vibe whose first answer omits `unmetPromises`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the prompt holds the compliance-review full schema, the argv holds no schema option, the refusal resumes the session once, and the retry's accepted answer is written

acceptanceCriteria.name: Every provider schema fits Codex strict
acceptanceCriteria.given: the full schema of every structured answer
acceptanceCriteria.when: the schema check derives and inspects each provider schema
acceptanceCriteria.then: each is a closed object with every key required, holds no lookahead pattern and no root `anyOf` or `oneOf`, carries `$schema` as a `const` wherever the answer has a `$schema`, and passes both Claude Code's and Codex strict's rules

acceptanceCriteria.name: A full schema change reaches the provider schema
acceptanceCriteria.given: a full schema that gains a required key in a test fixture
acceptanceCriteria.when: its provider schema is derived again
acceptanceCriteria.then: the provider schema requires the new key with no other edit

acceptanceCriteria.name: The provider schema never refuses an accepted answer
acceptanceCriteria.given: every answer fixture that phax's full schema accepts, for each structured answer and for the variant its call expects
acceptanceCriteria.when: each fixture is checked against its provider schema

acceptanceCriteria.name: The schema check names the bad construct
acceptanceCriteria.given: a full schema whose string field carries a lookahead pattern
acceptanceCriteria.then: it fails naming the answer and the lookahead pattern

acceptanceCriteria.name: structured_output is what phax decodes
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Claude Code result event whose `structured_output` holds a valid first-reading answer and whose `result` text is prose
acceptanceCriteria.when: the interactive first turn's outcome is read
acceptanceCriteria.then: phax accepts the `structured_output` answer and never parses the prose

acceptanceCriteria.name: A schema-valid answer can still be refused
acceptanceCriteria.given: a headless code review on Claude Code whose answer matches the provider schema but names criterion `ac-9`, absent from the source spec's sidecar
acceptanceCriteria.then: phax refuses the answer naming `ac-9`, prints the refusal and resumes the session once, and writes code-review.json only from an accepted retry

acceptanceCriteria.name: A code review refused twice fails
acceptanceCriteria.given: a headless code review whose first answer and retry are both refused
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits 1 naming both refusals and the retry command, and leaves code-review.json as it was

acceptanceCriteria.name: Provider retries exhausted is a session failure
acceptanceCriteria.given: a Claude Code authoring session that ends with an error result of subtype `error_max_structured_output_retries`
acceptanceCriteria.then: it prints `claude-code session failed (provider-error): error_max_structured_output_retries` and runs no corrective resume

acceptanceCriteria.name: An incomplete plan is reported inside the schema
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan.md whose Test strategy item is not in the line format, and an extraction answer with `plan: null` and an `incomplete` reason
acceptanceCriteria.when: the extraction fallback runs on Claude Code
acceptanceCriteria.then: the call carries the extraction provider schema and phax fails with `The extraction model found the plan incomplete:` followed by that reason

acceptanceCriteria.name: The compliance session writes nothing
acceptanceCriteria.given: a compliance review on Claude Code
acceptanceCriteria.then: the session is spawned read-only, nothing is written under the worktree's `.phax-context/`, and phax writes compliance-review.json and compliance-review.md in the run folder from the answer

acceptanceCriteria.name: The Markdown is the answer's rendering
acceptanceCriteria.when: phax writes compliance-review.md twice from it
acceptanceCriteria.then: both files are byte-identical and hold the verdict, the summary, one section per phase, `## Unplanned changes`, `## Unmet promises`, `## Attention points` and `## Pointers`, with `None.` for an empty list

acceptanceCriteria.name: A compliance answer must cover the run's phases
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run of phases phase-01 to phase-03 and a compliance answer whose perPhase names phase-01, phase-02 and phase-04
acceptanceCriteria.then: it refuses the answer naming phase-04 and the missing phase-03, and resumes the session once

acceptanceCriteria.name: No more unknown verdicts
acceptanceCriteria.given: a compliance review whose answer and retry are both refused
acceptanceCriteria.then: it prints `Compliance review failed: compliance-review answer rejected twice — first answer: …; retry: …` and the retry command, exits 1, writes neither compliance file nor a records entry, and never prints `Verdict: unknown`

acceptanceCriteria.name: compliance-review.json at 0.29.0
acceptanceCriteria.then: the file starts with `"$schema": "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/compliance-review/0.29.0.json"` and carries `unplannedChanges` and `unmetPromises`; a 0.29.0 file without `unmetPromises` is refused when read

arbitratedQuestions.question: If the smoke test shows that Claude Code's `--json-schema` does not work with `--resume`, `--tools` or stream-json for a given call, what does that call do on Claude Code?

options.label: That call, on Claude Code only, stays on the schema in the prompt plus phax's decoder and the corrective resume, like Vibe, and the per-provider table names it
options.abandons: One path for every structured call on Claude Code: the affected calls (likely decide's handback and every corrective resume) keep paying a corrective turn for shape mistakes.

options.label: The spec does not ship native structured output for that call on either provider until Claude Code supports the combination
options.abandons: Codex's native structured output for that call, which works today, held back for a Claude Code gap.

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: phax's decoder and the corrective resume already judge every answer, so a call left on the prompt schema loses only the saving, not correctness; holding Codex back for a Claude Code gap gives up a gain that is already there. The fallback is per call and per provider, named and tested, never silent.

verdict.why: phax's decoder and the corrective resume already judge every answer, so a call left on the prompt schema loses only the saving, not correctness; holding Codex back for a Claude Code gap gives up a gain that is already there. The fallback is per call and per provider, named and tested, never silent.
verdict.advocate: The strongest case for hold-the-call: one behavior per call across providers is easier to reason about, and a call that silently differs on Claude Code splits the test matrix and hides a gap that should be fixed upstream.

arbitratedQuestions.question: The compliance Markdown is now rendered by phax from the answer. What happens to the reviewer's free prose?

options.label: The Markdown is rendered from the answer's fields alone; the two ledgers become required fields; the only prose is the summary, the finding messages and the ledger notes
options.abandons: The reviewer's free narrative: any reasoning that fits no field, beyond the one-paragraph summary, is no longer kept.

options.label: The answer also carries a required `narrative` Markdown string that phax places verbatim after the verdict
options.abandons: A Markdown that is only a view of the checked answer: the narrative can contradict the verdict again, and the records keep a block of text no decoder can check.

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: The compliance review is advisory and read beside the verdict; what made it unreliable is prose that could disagree with the JSON. The ledgers were the structured part of that prose and become fields; the summary and per-finding messages keep room for the reviewer's words.

verdict.why: The compliance review is advisory and read beside the verdict; what made it unreliable is prose that could disagree with the JSON. The ledgers were the structured part of that prose and become fields; the summary and per-finding messages keep room for the reviewer's words.
verdict.advocate: The strongest case for narrative-field: a reviewer's reasoning often fits no field, and a required narrative keeps that judgment for the human reader instead of discarding it.

settled: Prerequisite: the spec "Provider failures" ships first; the structured answer is the answer side of its session outcome, and `error_max_structured_output_retries` stays its `provider-error`.
Two validations: the provider schema, enforced by Claude Code and Codex while generating, and phax's decoder (full schema plus coherence checks), the only judge on every provider.

One provider schema per structured answer, shared by Claude Code and Codex, fitting Codex strict: closed objects, every key required, no lookahead pattern, no root `anyOf`/`oneOf`, `$schema` as a `const`.
A root union whose variant the call already knows (hand-decision-answer for a spec or a plan) is narrowed to that variant in the provider schema; phax's decoder still decodes the full union.
The provider schema is derived from the full schema, never hand-written; keywords outside the strict subset are dropped from it and stay enforced by phax's decoder.
The prompt keeps stating the answer's full schema on every provider: the model must still know what the provider schema dropped.
Mistral Vibe stays on the prompt schema, phax's decoder and the corrective resume; its handling of `readOnly` is unchanged.
The corrective resume stays one, for every call that has a session; the headless code review and the compliance review gain it; the extraction fallback keeps one attempt.

The compliance session is read-only and returns its answer; phax writes compliance-review.json and compliance-review.md in the run folder; nothing is read from `.phax-context/`; `structuredVerdictMissing` and verdict `unknown` disappear.
compliance-review is stamped 0.29.0, with `unplannedChanges` and `unmetPromises` required, and the answer carries `$schema` in place of `version: 1`; no shims.
open: How the provider schema is derived from Effect's `JSONSchema.make` output (a transform over the exported schema, or a second annotation-driven export), as long as nothing is hand-written.
Where Codex's schema file is written (the session or decide folder is suggested) and how a large schema is passed inline to Claude Code.
The extraction answer's exact shape for its incomplete report (the `version: 2` with `plan` and `incomplete` sketch is indicative).
The ledger entries' exact keys, within q-compliance-prose.
Whether the schema check tests against the providers' own validators or a local encoding of their rules.
constraints: Target versions: Claude Code 2.1.311, Codex 0.153.4, Mistral Vibe 3.0.3.
Smoke-test Claude Code's `--json-schema` once per schema with `--resume`, with tools and with stream-json, in the real e2e tier; q-unsupported-combination decides what a failed combination does.
Every structured call goes through the Provider failures session-outcome reader; no call reads `finalText` once a structured answer is present.
The compliance-review format bump goes through packages/schemas snapshots and CURRENT_STAMPS like every persisted format; older compliance reviews are read only through the versioned history.
The full schemas `phax artifact schema` prints and packages/schemas publishes stay the contract; provider schemas are not published.
